title: Checkbox
summary: Native independent choices with grouped labeling, disabled support, and a synchronized indeterminate select-all state.
overview: A dependency-free checkbox recipe that preserves the native input and its established keyboard, form, validation, and high-contrast behavior.

component.useWhen: Use checkboxes when people may select zero, one, or several independent options.
component.avoidWhen: Avoid checkboxes for mutually exclusive choices, immediate on/off settings better expressed as switches, or commands that should be buttons.

examples.title: Checkbox group
examples.description: Select any combination of notification channels and observe the synchronized text summary.

source.html:
Notification channels

Selected: Email.

variants.title: Indeterminate select all
variants.summary: A parent checkbox whose mixed visual state reflects partially selected child options.
variants.useWhen: Use a select-all control when it applies to a clearly bounded set of related checkboxes.
variants.avoidWhen: Avoid it for paginated or partially loaded data unless the scope of all is explicit.
customization: Set the native indeterminate property in JavaScript because it has no HTML attribute.
The parent checked state means every child is selected; mixed means some but not all.
Recalculate after every child or parent change and after dynamic list updates.

example.title: Select notification channels
example.description: Toggle individual channels to produce the native mixed state, then use Select all to synchronize them.

source.html: Delivery channels

anatomy.name: Fieldset
anatomy.description: A semantic container for related independent choices.

anatomy.name: Legend
anatomy.description: The question or category shared by the group.

anatomy.name: Native input
anatomy.description: The focusable checkbox that owns checked, disabled, and indeterminate states.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: A clickable name with optional helper text.

accessibility: Keep the native checkbox in the accessibility tree and connect every input to a visible label.
Use fieldset and legend for a related group.
Do not use checked state to represent a partial group; set the indeterminate property.
Disabled checkboxes leave the tab sequence and must include an explanation when availability is not obvious.
Space toggles the focused native checkbox without custom keyboard code.
component.responsive: Labels wrap beside a fixed-size native control, and the group fills its container up to 30rem.
limitations: Indeterminate is a visual state and is not submitted as a distinct form value.
The select-all example assumes all children are present in the DOM.

provenance.label: Cross-library checkbox behavior study
provenance.note: Original native HTML, CSS, and JavaScript; no library source is copied.

title: Radio group
summary: A native mutually exclusive choice set with descriptive options and a responsive card presentation.
overview: A dependency-free radio group that relies on shared name attributes for selection and native arrow-key behavior.

component.useWhen: Use radio buttons when exactly one choice may be selected from a visible set of mutually exclusive options.
component.avoidWhen: Avoid them for independent choices, very long lists, or a single immediate on/off setting.

examples.title: Deployment region
examples.description: Move through the radios with arrow keys and observe the selected-region status.

source.html:
Deployment region

Selected region: US East.

variants.title: Choice cards
variants.summary: Radio options styled as responsive cards while preserving visible native controls and one shared group.
variants.useWhen: Use radio cards when each exclusive option needs a short description or price to support comparison.
variants.avoidWhen: Avoid them when options are simple labels; ordinary radios are faster to scan.
customization: The entire label is clickable while the native radio remains visible.
The checked card gains a strong border in addition to the radio state.
Cards collapse to one column below 38rem without changing keyboard or reading order.

example.title: Choose a plan
example.description: Select a plan from the responsive cards using pointer, Space, or arrow keys.

source.html: Choose a plan

anatomy.name: Fieldset
anatomy.description: The semantic boundary for one exclusive choice.

anatomy.name: Legend
anatomy.description: The question answered by the options.

anatomy.name: Native radio
anatomy.description: The focusable selection control sharing one name with its siblings.

anatomy.name: Option label
anatomy.description: The choice name and optional concise description.

accessibility: Group related radios with fieldset and legend.
Give every radio the same name and a unique value.
Keep the native input visible or visually hidden without removing it from the accessibility tree.
Browsers provide arrow-key movement and selection within a named group.
Do not preselect an option when no default is genuinely appropriate.
component.responsive: The basic group remains stacked. Choice cards use three columns when space allows and one column below 38rem.
limitations: The demo does not submit a form or persist the chosen value.
Card styling uses :has(), which requires a current browser; selection remains usable without it.

provenance.label: Cross-library radio behavior study
provenance.note: Original native HTML, CSS, and JavaScript; no library source is copied.

title: Switch
summary: An immediate native on/off setting styled as a switch with explicit state feedback and reduced motion.
overview: A dependency-free switch built on a native checkbox with role=switch. It is reserved for settings that take effect immediately, not form answers awaiting submission.

component.useWhen: Use a switch for a binary setting that takes effect immediately when toggled.
component.avoidWhen: Avoid switches for selecting items, agreeing to terms, submitting a command, or choosing among more than two values.

examples.title: Immediate setting
examples.description: Toggle automatic backups with pointer or Space and observe the explicit status update.

source.html: Automatic backups are on.

variants.title: Settings list
variants.summary: Several independent switches presented as a structured list with disabled-state context.
variants.useWhen: Use a settings list when several independent immediate preferences belong to one section.
variants.avoidWhen: Avoid using switches as a substitute for a multi-select form that is saved only after submission.
customization: Each row is its own label and maintains a minimum comfortable target.
Disabled settings include visible text explaining why they are unavailable.
Do not add a group role unless the collection has a shared accessible label.

example.title: Privacy settings
example.description: Toggle the available preferences and inspect the disabled setting with its explanation.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: The stable name of the setting.

anatomy.name: Description
anatomy.description: Optional consequences or scope of changing the setting.

anatomy.name: Native input
anatomy.description: A checkbox with role=switch that owns focus and checked state.

anatomy.name: Track and thumb
anatomy.description: CSS visuals driven by native checked and disabled states.

accessibility: Use role=switch on the native checkbox so checked state is announced as on or off.
Keep a visible label that remains stable when the state changes.
Use Space to toggle through native checkbox behavior.
Pair disabled settings with a visible reason.
Do not put On or Off inside the accessible name; state is announced separately.
component.responsive: Rows keep text and the fixed-size switch in two columns; descriptions wrap without shrinking the control.
limitations: Custom switch appearance depends on appearance:none; the native checkbox semantics remain intact.
The example emits state changes but does not persist them or handle save failures.

provenance.label: Cross-library switch behavior study
provenance.note: Original native HTML, CSS, and JavaScript; no library source is copied.

title: Text field
summary: A labeled native text input with helper text, character counting, and an accessible validation-error state.
overview: A dependency-free text field that keeps label, purpose, constraints, helper text, and errors explicit around a native input.

component.useWhen: Use a text field for short free-form values that fit on one line.
component.avoidWhen: Avoid it for known option sets, long prose, formatted rich content, or data better collected by a purpose-specific native input type.

examples.title: Field with character count
examples.description: Enter a project name and observe the count without changing the input's stable accessible name.

source.html: Use a short name your team will recognize.0 / 40

variants.title: Validation error
variants.summary: A submit-time invalid state with linked error text, focus recovery, and native email validation.
variants.useWhen: Use an invalid state after validation has run and the user needs a specific correction.
variants.avoidWhen: Avoid showing errors before the person has had a reasonable chance to complete the field.
customization: aria-invalid changes only after validation and clears once the value becomes valid.
The persistent description and conditional error both appear in aria-describedby.
Failed submission moves focus to the first invalid field in this compact example.

example.title: Email validation
example.description: Submit an empty or malformed email, then correct it and observe the linked error clear.

source.html:
We will send the receipt to this address.

Enter a complete email address such as name@example.com.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: A visible, stable name connected with for and id.

anatomy.name: Native input
anatomy.description: The control carrying type, name, autocomplete, required, and value.

anatomy.name: Helper text
anatomy.description: Persistent format or purpose guidance connected with aria-describedby.

anatomy.name: Error
anatomy.description: Specific correction guidance shown only after validation.

accessibility: Every field needs a persistent visible label; placeholder text is not a replacement.
Choose the most specific native input type and autocomplete token available.
Connect helper and error text with aria-describedby.
Set aria-invalid only after validation has identified a problem.
Keep character counts outside the label so the accessible name remains stable.
component.responsive: Fields fill their container up to 32rem. Helper metadata stacks below 32rem to avoid cramped wrapping.
limitations: Native email validity rules are intentionally broad and do not prove that an address exists.
The recipe demonstrates one field; full forms need ordered error handling across every invalid control.

provenance.label: Cross-library text input study
provenance.note: Original native HTML, CSS, and JavaScript; no library source is copied.

title: Select
summary: A labeled native single-select with placeholder guidance, grouped options, and synchronized feedback.
overview: A dependency-free select that preserves the platform picker, mobile presentation, keyboard type-ahead, form submission, and optgroup semantics.

component.useWhen: Use a native select for one choice from a moderate, known list where seeing every option at once is not necessary.
component.avoidWhen: Avoid it for very few options that radios can expose, large searchable datasets, or multiple free-form values.

examples.title: Single select
examples.description: Choose a timezone using the native picker and observe the synchronized visible status.

source.html:
Dates will be displayed in this timezone.

No timezone selected.

variants.title: Grouped options
variants.summary: A native select organized with optgroup labels for a longer but still manageable list.
variants.useWhen: Use optgroups when meaningful categories make a moderate option list easier to scan.
variants.avoidWhen: Avoid deeply nested taxonomies or hundreds of options; use a purpose-built searchable picker instead.
customization: Optgroup labels describe categories but are not selectable values.
Keep option labels understandable outside their group when the chosen value is displayed later.
The placeholder remains disabled so it cannot become a submitted choice.

example.title: Grouped deployment region
example.description: Open the native picker and scan regions grouped by continent.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: A visible name connected to the select.

anatomy.name: Native select
anatomy.description: The focusable picker and submitted form control.

anatomy.name: Placeholder option
anatomy.description: A disabled prompt when no default is appropriate.

anatomy.name: Option group
anatomy.description: An optional labeled category for related choices.

anatomy.name: Helper text
anatomy.description: Persistent context connected with aria-describedby.

accessibility: Connect every select to a visible label.
Use a disabled placeholder only when no valid default exists.
Keep option labels concise and unique.
Use optgroup for one meaningful category level only.
Do not replace the native picker solely to control popup styling.
component.responsive: The select fills its container and uses the operating system's native narrow-screen picker.
limitations: Native option popup styling varies by browser and operating system.
This component does not provide search, multi-select chips, remote loading, or virtualization.

provenance.label: Cross-library select behavior study
provenance.note: Original native HTML, CSS, and JavaScript; no library source is copied.

title: Tabs
summary: A manual-activation tab set with complete ARIA relationships, roving focus, and a responsive vertical variant.
overview: A dependency-free tabs pattern for switching among peer views in the same context. It distinguishes focus from selection in the default manual-activation model.

component.useWhen: Use tabs for a small set of peer sections where only one panel needs to be visible and switching should not navigate to a new URL.
component.avoidWhen: Avoid tabs for sequential steps, primary site navigation, content people need to compare simultaneously, or headings that should remain searchable on one page.

examples.title: Manual activation tabs
examples.description: Use Left/Right, Home, and End to move focus; press Enter or Space to reveal the focused panel.

source.html:

variants.title: Vertical tabs
variants.summary: A left-aligned tab list with automatic Up/Down activation that collapses to a horizontal list on narrow screens.
variants.useWhen: Use vertical tabs when labels need more width and panel changes are immediate enough for automatic activation.
variants.avoidWhen: Avoid automatic activation when switching triggers network work, heavy rendering, or a disruptive context change.
customization: aria-orientation=vertical tells assistive technology to expect Up and Down navigation.
Focus and selection move together because every panel is already available locally.
Below 38rem the visual list becomes horizontal; keyboard behavior remains Up/Down, so use the default variant if orientation must change semantically too.

example.title: Vertical settings tabs
example.description: Use Up/Down, Home, and End to move and activate tabs, then inspect the stacked narrow-screen layout.

anatomy.name: Tab list
anatomy.description: The composite control containing peer tabs.

anatomy.name: Tab
anatomy.description: A button with selection state and a reference to one panel.

anatomy.name: Panel
anatomy.description: The content region labeled by its controlling tab.

anatomy.name: Roving focus
anatomy.description: Only the selected tab participates in ordinary Tab navigation.

accessibility: Use role=tablist, role=tab, and role=tabpanel only for dynamic same-page views.
Connect every tab and panel bidirectionally with aria-controls and aria-labelledby.
Keep exactly one tab selected and in the tab order.
Manual activation uses arrows for focus and Enter or Space for selection.
Do not use tab semantics for navigation links that load another route.
component.responsive: The horizontal list scrolls within its surface. Vertical tabs become a one-column visual layout below 38rem.
limitations: The vertical variant keeps vertical keyboard semantics after its narrow visual reflow; choose the default pattern when this mismatch is undesirable.
Tabs do not update the URL, preserve deep links, or lazy-load panels.

provenance.label: Cross-library tabs behavior study
provenance.note: Original native HTML, CSS, and JavaScript; no library source is copied.
